mechanism: DOCUMENTARY_VALIDATED. FINRA Rule 11140(b)(2) continues to define the ex-date for qualifying large distributions as the first business day after the payable date, and FINRA guidance explains that sellers before that ex-date may have to relinquish the distribution to purchasers. Current Nasdaq corporate-action notices demonstrate live use of due-bill redemption dates and, in at least one 2026 case, a separate when-issued line explicitly stripped of the special cash dividend entitlement.
data_integrity: PASS_FOR_TEST_DESIGN_AT_DOCUMENTARY_LEVEL_WITH_EVENT_SPECIFIC_GATE. The governing rule is public and current rulemaking materials preserve the >=25% branch. For listed securities the actual exchange corporate-action notice must control the selected event rather than a researcher inferring treatment from size alone. The minimum event record must freeze source publication time, issuer/security/CUSIP, distribution terms, record/payable/ex/due-bill dates and any when-issued/ex-distribution symbol before price access. Later amendments to amounts or transaction closing must be versioned rather than silently substituted.
statistical: NOT_TESTED_AND_NOT_AUTHORIZED. No prices, spreads, returns, hit rates, sample means or event-study outcomes were read. A future sample must be generated mechanically from documentary eligibility, not selected from remembered profitable special dividends.
economic: UNTESTED. Due-bill mechanics prove an unusual entitlement clock, not a mispricing. Arbitrage desks, DTC processing, short-sale dividend obligations, taxes, borrow, corporate-action fees and when-issued liquidity may fully enforce parity. Any future test must model the exact cash/stock entitlement and all operational frictions.
prospective: NONE. No prospective market observation was performed or authorized.
operational_readiness: READY_FOR_FROZEN_TEST_DESIGN_ONLY. A clean first design should compare contractually equivalent entitlement-bearing and non-entitlement-bearing claims only where the exchange itself publishes both legs or otherwise provides unambiguous entitlement semantics. Ordinary large-dividend stock-only direction is too confounded by underlying business/transaction news and should not be the primary expression.
reason: The event definition survives independent documentary challenge and is distinct from the pinned Legacy families. The strongest version is narrower than 'large dividend anomaly': it is an entitlement-parity/event-microstructure hypothesis anchored to official due-bill and when-issued mechanics. Current FINRA and Nasdaq evidence establish the mechanism and point-in-time event clock without outcome access. The next legitimate action is a predeclared test/data contract, not a return lookup.
scope_of_falsification: This assessment validates only rule/event mechanics and testability. It does not support positive expected return, direction, capacity or broker accessibility. A future null/negative test would falsify the exact frozen entitlement-parity expression, not the legal existence of due bills.
